specReviews.primaryContract: Inspector Phase controls remain usable within both supported viewport widths; Group-color inheritance is reversible, unavailable for Ungrouped Transactions, and does not create History before Apply.
specReviews.reason: The test combines a real Group-color interaction with a compact Inspector fit invariant at two widths; this cross-panel UI contract is not established by a unit test.

specReviews.primaryContract: Inspector and Bottom Phases controls share one unapplied draft and one Apply creates a single History unit.
specReviews.reason: This is a distinct cross-surface Draft/Apply production journey; unit state tests alone cannot prove both editors show the same draft.

specReviews.primaryContract: Multiple Bottom row edits commit together through Apply as one Undoable semantic operation, while rejected Apply leaves Canonical/History unchanged and explains the validation failure.
specReviews.reason: This protects the actual table editing boundary plus command/history outcome; lower-level tests should complement but not replace the visible Apply journey.

specReviews.primaryContract: Transaction table headers remain readable/aligned with the body, color is represented in the Color column, and the table fits both supported viewports without page overflow.
specReviews.reason: The two viewport variants directly protect responsive table width and typography, which is an explicit width-dependent visual contract.

specReviews.primaryContract: Visible icon-only controls expose accessible names/tooltips and menu/dialog actions expose their interaction semantics across Cycle, Transaction, and Combined; hover help is view-only.
specReviews.reason: This cross-mode accessibility and command-affordance matrix is a distinct UI contract. It currently inspects the rendered control surface directly; retain it while cheaper independent coverage is assessed, not as a duplicate of keyboard navigation tests.

specReviews.primaryContract: Visible interactive controls communicate pointer/editability and disabled state consistently across Cycle, Transaction, and Combined.
specReviews.reason: The suite asserts cursor and disabled-reason affordances, a different invariant from accessible naming and mode-specific keyboard undo/redo. Viewport variants are retained pending measured runtime and compact-layout coupling review.

specReviews.primaryContract: Transaction and Annotation drags visibly explain Escape cancellation, clear the hint after cancellation/release, and preserve Canonical/History on cancel.
specReviews.reason: A real pointer gesture is required to verify the transient status feedback and cancel/release lifecycle; the two Transaction viewport cases guard responsive gesture hit targets.

specReviews.primaryContract: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo one semantic edit consistently in Cycle, Transaction, and Combined.
specReviews.reason: The three modes have distinct command surfaces and the user-visible keyboard route is the contract; this is one parameterized journey per mode, not viewport duplication.

specReviews.primaryContract: Disabled Bottom Transaction commands explain why they are unavailable.
specReviews.reason: This is the specific Transaction Bottom command state, complementary to the cross-mode disabled-cursor audit and suitable for a focused user-visible gate.

specReviews.primaryContract: Ribbon menu, dialog, and immediate actions remain visually/semantically distinguishable at desktop and compact widths.
specReviews.reason: The two viewports are intentional because ribbon density and overflow can alter the visible affordance distinction at compact width.

specReviews.primaryContract: Bottom Start sort direction changes only view order, preserves selection-independent canonical/history state, and returning to document order restores the original row sequence.
specReviews.reason: This overlaps the broader #747 Start/End sort matrix but uniquely asserts restoring exact document row order; keep this invariant until it is merged into the domain contract suite.

specReviews.primaryContract: Click/Ctrl/Shift/Ctrl+A operate on the Bottom row selection set without checkboxes; Duplicate acts on the selected set as one History unit and Undo restores the original count.
specReviews.reason: This exercises bulk mutation and one-step undo in addition to selection grammar, unlike the selection-only compact journey; preserve both contracts.

specReviews.primaryContract: Bottom grid supports click/Ctrl/Shift selection, visible-order ranges under filtering, Ctrl+A scoped away from text inputs, and accessible selected/disclosure state without Canonical/History changes.
specReviews.reason: Retain one compact viewport for viewport-independent selection semantics; the removed desktop duplicate is mapped in qa/test-consolidation-map.json and responsive geometry remains tested at both viewports by #747 geometry acceptance.

specReviews.primaryContract: Start/End ascending/descending are announced accessibly, one sort key is active, sorting preserves selected ID and view-only state, and the Bottom settings gear opens/closes with Escape.
specReviews.reason: This is broader than #737's Start-only sorting contract and adds End sorting/settings accessibility. One compact viewport is enough for these semantic assertions; two-view responsive geometry remains in the dedicated #747 geometry acceptance.

specReviews.primaryContract: Follow Selection and Pin are reachable in Bottom settings; Pin changes follow status and survives closing the popover with Escape.
specReviews.reason: A real popover/action journey is needed to verify the production path and persisted view state; the geometry suite measures placement separately.

specReviews.primaryContract: Settings, selection, sort, and Phase expansion preserve the table header position and align child Phase cells with semantic columns at both supported viewport sizes, without document/history changes.
specReviews.reason: The assertions measure responsive panel/header/cell geometry, so both 1280x720 and 1672x941 remain necessary; this suite also replaces the viewport-only geometry coverage removed from semantic tests.

specReviews.primaryContract: During real native horizontal scrolling, Cycle fixed columns stay stationary and visible while the Timeline advances; Canonical, History, and Dirty remain unchanged.
specReviews.reason: This observes the real native scrollbar and user-visible fixed-column behavior at two widths because responsive geometry and native thumb hit area are width-dependent. It replaces the synthetic-width/DOM-ancestry E2E variant while a static architecture guard checks CSS ownership.

specReviews.primaryContract: The Cycle-only scroll split does not shift visible workspace geometry in Cycle, Transaction, or Combined beyond 1px, excluding the documented Cycle-span and Transaction-compression differences.
specReviews.reason: It protects a cross-mode geometry compatibility contract against a hand-authored pre-split reference at both approved viewport sizes; it is layout-specific and belongs outside the ordinary focused PR journey.

specReviews.primaryContract: During real horizontal scrolling, no time-domain pixels intrude beneath the fixed Cycle columns and the timeline scrollbar remains aligned with the time-domain region.
specReviews.reason: This is a distinct pixel-level no-bleed visual contract with screenshot sampling during the drag at both width-dependent layouts; keep it in the visual tier rather than duplicating it in semantic PR tests.

specReviews.primaryContract: Analytic LocalGeometry returns the same cycle-boundary, transition, threshold, edge, and value-start anchors as the independent WaveDrom SVG extractor across representative signal tokens and rebased windows.
specReviews.reason: This browser probe is needed to compare two independently produced geometry maps (analytic production source versus real WaveDrom SVG extraction); pure unit tests cannot prove parity with the renderer. It subsumes the narrower cycle-only equivalence spec without duplicating the production pitch formula.

specReviews.primaryContract: After a real 10,000-cycle document far-scroll, the actual rendered waveform surface bounds cover the timeline viewport.
specReviews.reason: This large-document user-visible geometry journey is expensive and protects viewport coverage after a far jump; its assertion measures the rendered SVG/Canvas surface rectangle rather than internal inline left/width values.

reviews.title: Annotation Preview Update reverts even without an explicit Cancel, when selection moves away
reviews.primaryContract: A transient annotation preview is removed when selection changes, without mutating canonical state.
reviews.reason: The annotation overlay preview lifecycle is user-visible and owner-specific; the similar Clock test exercises a different renderer and draft owner, so title similarity is not duplicate coverage.

reviews.title: Clock Preview reverts even without an explicit Cancel, when selection moves away
reviews.primaryContract: A transient Clock waveform preview is removed when selection changes, without mutating canonical state.
reviews.reason: The Clock waveform preview uses a distinct renderer and draft owner from annotation overlay preview; keep the independent visible regression journey.

reviews.title: Apply commits the previewed draft as one real SemanticCommand
reviews.primaryContract: Applying a previewed Annotation draft commits the same values through one semantic command.
reviews.reason: The visually similar Clock test protects a separate editor and waveform projection; it does not replace Annotation command application coverage.

reviews.title: Apply after Preview commits exactly the previewed draft as one real SemanticCommand
reviews.primaryContract: Applying a previewed Clock draft commits the previewed generator through one semantic command.
reviews.reason: The Annotation counterpart cannot prove Clock waveform preview/application equivalence, so retain both product journeys.

reviews.title: Bottom Editor splitter resizes and collapses without changing document or render state
reviews.primaryContract: Bottom splitter interaction changes panel size/visibility without Canonical, History, Dirty, or render-session changes.
reviews.reason: Inspector resize is a similar gesture but has a different axis, owner, state, and layout consequence; a shared low-level drag unit test would not replace this observable contract.

reviews.title: Inspector splitter resizes and collapses without changing document or render state
reviews.primaryContract: Inspector splitter interaction changes panel width/visibility without Canonical, History, Dirty, or render-session changes.
reviews.reason: Bottom resize differs in orientation and layout owner; keep this as the user-visible inspector-specific journey rather than merging by title similarity.

reviews.title: Transaction Open reaches first useful paint for small fixture at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: Small Transaction document open reaches useful Transaction projection at compact viewport.
reviews.reason: This is a small-fixture baseline at compact viewport; it differs in fixture size and purpose from the separate 500-Transaction scalability budget test. Runtime has not yet been measured.

reviews.title: Transaction Open reaches first useful paint for small fixture at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: Small Transaction document open reaches useful Transaction projection at desktop viewport.
reviews.reason: Desktop viewport is retained as a responsive/performance comparison against 1280x720; runtime has not yet been measured.

reviews.title: Transaction Open reaches first useful paint for medium fixture at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: Medium Transaction document open reaches useful Transaction projection at compact viewport.
reviews.reason: Medium fixture adds a scale point to the startup curve, not duplicate acceptance of the 500-Transaction case. Runtime has not yet been measured.

reviews.title: Transaction Open reaches first useful paint for medium fixture at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: Medium Transaction document open reaches useful Transaction projection at desktop viewport.
reviews.reason: Desktop viewport is retained as a responsive/performance comparison against 1280x720; runtime has not yet been measured.

reviews.title: 500-Transaction Open reaches first useful Transaction paint at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: A large Transaction document produces a non-zero visible bar projection after Open.
reviews.reason: This is the large-scale stress point with its own 500-Transaction fixture and explicit scalability assertions; it is not a duplicate of small/medium startup checks. Runtime has not yet been measured.

reviews.title: 500-Transaction Open reaches first useful Transaction paint at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: A large Transaction document produces a non-zero visible bar projection at compact viewport.
reviews.reason: Compact viewport stresses available workspace and row projection separately from desktop; runtime has not yet been measured.

reviews.title: J1-3 fresh -> Cycle: renders, view-only, no errors
reviews.primaryContract: A fresh application can enter Cycle mode without changing Canonical, History, or Dirty state and without runtime errors.
reviews.reason: Representative fresh-state Cycle entry journey; complementary Transaction and Combined entries are also retained in the same product lifecycle contract suite.

reviews.title: J1-3 fresh -> Transaction: renders, view-only, no errors
reviews.primaryContract: A fresh application can enter Transaction mode without changing Canonical, History, or Dirty state and without runtime errors.
reviews.reason: Transaction workspace has a separate initialization/projection path, so this user-visible mode entry complements Cycle and Combined smoke journeys.

reviews.title: J1-3 fresh -> Combined: renders, view-only, no errors
reviews.primaryContract: A fresh application can enter Combined mode without changing Canonical, History, or Dirty state and without runtime errors.
reviews.reason: Combined composes two view owners and needs its own real startup journey; this is not covered by either single mode.

reviews.title: J4/J16 Cycle -> Transaction -> Combined -> Cycle, then rapid switching, stays view-only and error-free
reviews.primaryContract: Mode transitions and rapid switching preserve document/history state and keep the application error-free.
reviews.reason: This is the direct cross-mode lifecycle invariant and exercises state transitions that static/unit tests cannot fully prove.

reviews.title: J5/J10 select -> edit -> Apply -> Undo -> Redo, and an unapplied draft does not leak to the next selection
reviews.primaryContract: Selection changes discard an unapplied draft; Apply creates one history step and Undo/Redo restore the committed state.
reviews.reason: This production journey covers cross-selection draft isolation plus the visible Apply/Undo/Redo contract, which is not reducible to a single unit invariant.

reviews.title: J9 Bottom follows the selected entity kind
reviews.primaryContract: Bottom panel follows the selected entity kind across the actual application surface.
reviews.reason: The selected entity kind drives a cross-surface panel contract that is appropriately verified at the UI boundary.

reviews.title: Transaction tree selection opens the selected canonical transaction in Inspector
reviews.primaryContract: Selecting a Transaction in the Tree selects that same canonical entity in Inspector and applies edits to it.
reviews.reason: This is the focused Transaction selection/Inspector production route and is a small changed-domain browser journey.

reviews.title: #554 from-scratch Transaction workspace journey at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: Production-path Transaction creation, group/link edits, selection sync, Undo/Redo, mode round trips, and Save/New/Open preserve semantic data.
reviews.reason: This is a broad end-to-end lifecycle with real file save/open and many semantic operations. Keep out of ordinary focused PR verification, but retain as automated integration acceptance.

reviews.title: #554 from-scratch Transaction workspace journey at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: The same production-path Transaction lifecycle remains usable at a compact viewport while semantic edits survive Save/New/Open.
reviews.reason: The journey exercises responsive panel geometry and overflow-sensitive controls at 1280x720; the desktop variant is not a substitute for this width-specific contract.

reviews.title: locks v8 badge, display, MiniMap, and bottom-toolbar geometry
reviews.primaryContract: Role badge/frozen-column alignment, toolbar control grouping, and MiniMap stability remain within approved visual geometry.
reviews.reason: This single desktop geometry contract checks measurable visual relationships rather than a broad screenshot matrix; it belongs in the visual profile, not every semantic PR journey.
